assessments.quote: This paper evaluates the performance of segmentation foundation models (FMs), including Segment Anything Model (SAM), MedSAM, and UniverSeg, against traditional supervised learning (with nnU-net) for lymphoma segmentation
assessments.reason: Head-to-head benchmark of MedSAM vs nnU-Net on clinical MRI segmentation, reporting that supervised nnU-Net outperformed foundation models; directly evidences both methods and their comparative difference.

assessments.quote: This study compares three methods for 2D bone metastasis segmentation on computed tomography slices-the self-configuring nnU-Net pipeline, a fine-tuned DINOv3 foundation model, and a prompt-free MedSAM foundation model adaptation
assessments.reason: Direct comparative evaluation of MedSAM and nnU-Net under comparable conditions with Dice/NHD results, showing nnU-Net higher Dice and lower NHD; provides concrete performance differences.

assessments.quote: An nnU-Net model was trained from scratch to serve as a benchmark and to provide bounding box prompts for MedSAM.
assessments.reason: Evaluates off-the-shelf MedSAM against an nnU-Net benchmark on pelvic MRI, discussing prompt dependence and fine-tuning needs; directly compares the two methods and their differing requirements.

assessments.quote: two contemporary segmentation frameworks, nnU-Net v2 and MedSAM
assessments.reason: Trains and evaluates nnU-Net v2 and MedSAM on cardiac MRE segmentation, comparing input representations and automation strategies; directly evidences both methods and their comparative behavior.

assessments.quote: This research uses Segment Anything Model (SAM), Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), MedSAM, SAM-Med-3D, and nnU-Net to obtain zero-shot inference on the BraTS 2023 adult glioma and pediatrics dataset
assessments.reason: Benchmarks MedSAM and nnU-Net across prompt qualities on brain tumour data, noting nnU-Net remains dominant due to prompt impracticality; directly compares the two methods.

assessments.quote: we present a novel approach which integrates self-configuring segmentation frameworks (nnU-net) with generalized foundation models (MedSAM)
assessments.reason: Compares integrated MedSAM-nnU-Net against MedSAM and nnU-Net individually on pelvic MRI, reporting improvements; directly evidences both methods and their comparative performance.

assessments.quote: It includes: MedSAM zero-shot and MedSAM+LoRA adapters; crop-guided and prompt-matched nnU-Net export
assessments.reason: Software release description mentioning MedSAM and nnU-Net components, but no abstract-level comparative results or analysis; only indirect evidence.

assessments.quote: We evaluated SAM-Med3D for ESCC lesion segmentation and compared it with state-of-the-art methods including nnU-Net, SegVol, and MedSAM.
assessments.reason: Reports nnU-Net and MedSAM as baselines with Dice/HD95 in an ESCC segmentation study, but the focus is SAM-Med3D optimization rather than a dedicated MedSAM vs nnU-Net comparison.

assessments.quote: Here we present MedSAM, a foundation model designed for bridging this gap by enabling universal medical image segmentation.
assessments.reason: Original MedSAM framework paper providing evidence for the MedSAM side, but it does not address nnU-Net or compare the two methods.

assessments.quote: We systematically evaluate six diverse architectures spanning 2D CNNs (U-Net, MedSAM) to 3D volumetric models (nnU-Net, UNETR, Total Segmentator, MIScnn) on the KiTS19 dataset
assessments.reason: Evaluates MedSAM and nnU-Net among six architectures on kidney tumor CT with Dice and computational analysis, but the primary aim is clinical feasibility/false-positive analysis rather than a focused MedSAM vs nnU-Net comparison.

assessments.quote: Tumor multi-region segmentation was conducted using nnU-Net, followed by extraction of VASARI features and ADC-related parameters.
assessments.reason: nnU-Net is used only as a segmentation tool for downstream glioma subtype prediction; no MedSAM evidence and no comparison of the two methods.
